rows.en: Daimos, Battle Tuuurn!!
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required. Root confirmed Battle Turn stem using Akurasu MX BGM List; elongated vowel preserves the cry.

rows.en: Uoooh! Nnngh! Haaah!! Daaaaiiiimoooos!!
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required.

rows.en: Ngh!? He's here too!?
rows.notes: He is Kazuya, revealed by Daimos transformation immediately before this line; gender supported by glossary.

rows.en: You've come to take back your woman, Kazuya Ryuzaki...
rows.notes: Hokushin addresses Kazuya about reclaiming Erika; full source name preserved.

rows.en: I've come back, just as I promised! To take Erika back into my own hands!!
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required.

rows.en: My lady, look over there! It's Kazuya! It's Daimos!!
rows.notes: Margarete addresses princess Erika with nursemaid title; look is imperative to Erika. Root confirmed My lady as ordinary honorific translation supported by Erika princess profile.

rows.en: Oh, Kazuya...!
rows.notes: Vocative with emotional Oh; checked both initial rescue encouragement294 and reunion367.

rows.en: Kazuya, are you going to settle things with him?
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required.

rows.en: No... I'll leave Hokushin to him.
rows.notes: Him is Akito; source uses pronoun, duel context251..259 and127..128 settle referent.
Nonverbal surprise retained.

rows.en: You're sure you're all right with that?
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required.

rows.en: Yes... Compared to his anguish and suffering, I...
rows.notes: Unfinished I... retained exactly; source omits the comparison predicate deliberately.
uncertain: Retained source unfinished clause or purpose fragment; not grammatical pro-drop.

rows.en: That's why... as a man, I want to let him settle things with Hokushin...!
rows.notes: Man-to-man solidarity motivates letting Akito settle the duel with Hokushin; subject restored.

rows.en: Big brother...
rows.notes: Nana affectionate address to Kazuya; source kinship vocative retained without asserting biological siblinghood.

rows.en: But I won't show any mercy to anyone else...!
rows.notes: Anyone else means enemies except Hokushin, not allies.

rows.en: I'll crush their new order with my own fists!!
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required.

rows.en: Kazuya... I believed you'd come back for me, no matter what...!
rows.notes: Erika speaks to Kazuya, who returned to rescue her.

rows.en: Erika...!
rows.notes: Vocative checked both305 and364; reunion and initial exchange share the same exclamation.

rows.en: ...I understand. You want me to rescue Yurika Misumaru, don't you...?
rows.notes: Erika understands Kazuya is asking her to rescue Yurika, confirmed by135 acceptance136 and safe rescue report373.

rows.en: I'm counting on you, Erika. I want all his suffering over these three whole years to be rewarded.
rows.notes: Kazuya asks Erika for help. He wants Akito rewarded after three years suffering; does not ask Akito to rescue Erika.

rows.en: Yes...
rows.notes: Context verified in full owning event; spoken subject/verb restored where required.

rows.en: My lady...
rows.notes: Margarete addresses Erika by princess/nursemaid title. Root confirmed My lady as ordinary honorific translation supported by Erika princess profile.

rows.en: Let's go, Margarete. To carry out our final duty...
rows.notes: Erika addresses Margarete; source purpose clause is retained as an appended fragment, leading into139.
uncertain: Retained source unfinished clause or purpose fragment; not grammatical pro-drop.

rows.en: To save the lovers torn apart by a cruel fate...!
rows.notes: Purpose-clause fragment deliberately continues138; lovers are Akito/Yurika.
uncertain: Retained source unfinished clause or purpose fragment; not grammatical pro-drop.

rows.notes: Silence at all three uses: introduction, Saiga's Mokuren suspicion, and Kazuya's defiance.

rows.en: ...Guh... Well... done...
rows.notes: Hokushin defeated by Akito; follows reused silences at s0930:312-313. Dying cough and grudging praise.

rows.en: You must be afraid... You must be bitter...! Even clad in armor... you cannot protect the weakness in your heart!
rows.notes: Hokushin taunts Akito after defeat; armor cannot shield psychological weakness. You/your restored.
Akito reacts wordlessly to Hokushin; preserve emphatic silence.

rows.en: Your coup has failed, and we have taken control of the system! Surrender without a fight!
rows.notes: Kazuya challenges Kusakabe during conditional battle exchange. We controls system; command directed to enemy.

rows.en: It is not over yet...! Everything begins with this battle!
rows.notes: Kusakabe rejects Kazuya surrender demand; this battle starts the new order.

rows.en: How many human lives have been taken for the ideals you preach!?
rows.notes: Kazuya accuses Kusakabe of deaths caused by professed ideals.

rows.en: No matter what pretty words you dress it up in, I will not accept it... I will never accept a war that brings sorrow and tears!!
rows.notes: Kazuya refuses wars causing sorrow and tears, whatever their rhetorical justification.

rows.en: Tell him, Kyoshiro! Give him one of your usual maxims!
rows.notes: Nana asks Kyoshiro to address Kusakabe with his customary maxim; direction remains listener acting.

rows.en: I have no words left for this man...
rows.notes: Kyoshiro says he has nothing further to tell Kusakabe; I restored.

rows.en: But I will say this anyway!
rows.notes: Kyoshiro nevertheless introduces his maxim.

rows.en: In the words of the departed: "The government is the sail, the people the wind, the state the ship, and the age the sea." Borne's words!
rows.notes: Kyoshiro quotes deceased Borne. All four mappings preserved; no biographical addition. Semantic precision: remove the added descriptor thinker; source merely invokes a deceased author and names Borne.
uncertain: Borne attribution follows root primary-source verification; source calls the deceased author by surname only.

rows.en: You set sail on the great sea of the age without the wind of the people! Only destruction awaits you!
rows.notes: Kyoshiro applies the quote to Kusakabe and followers; popular support is wind, age the sea.

rows.en: Alien! You could never understand... our ideals... our aspirations!
rows.notes: Kusakabe dismisses alien Rom as incapable of understanding their ideals and aspirations.

rows.en: ...The tears of the people will someday become a river of sorrow and flow into a sea of tragedy...
rows.notes: Rom solemnly extends water imagery; people tears become sorrow river then tragedy sea.

rows.en: How many tears do you think will be shed in this world because of you!?
rows.notes: Rom accuses Kusakabe and followers of causing worldly tears.

rows.en: All are sacrifices to build a better world... I will not let that pain go to waste!
rows.notes: Kusakabe defends sacrifice for a better world and promises not to waste pain.

rows.en: If you proclaim an ideal, seek a path that requires none of those sacrifices! That is what true governance means!!
rows.notes: Rom says real governance pursues ideals without even those sacrifices; listener commanded to find path.

rows.en: Here I come, Kusakabe! I'll settle the score from the Lizard War... and avenge Tsukumo, all right here!!
rows.notes: Ryoko threatens Kusakabe with repayment for Lizard War and revenge for Tsukumo; both retained.

rows.en: Coups are so out of style! This is an age when everyone wants to live in peace!
rows.notes: Hikaru criticizes coup as outdated in an era of people wanting peaceful lives.

rows.en: ...Enough already. All you do is repeat the same tragedies.
rows.notes: Izumi tells enemy faction to stop repeating tragedy.

rows.en: Lieutenant General Kusakabe, it's about time you called it quits.
rows.notes: Saburota addresses Kusakabe respectfully but flippantly; source explicit rank retained.

rows.en: That voice... Takasugi... You too have changed...
rows.notes: Kusakabe recognizes Saburota by surname Takasugi and comments on change.

rows.en: You don't seem to have changed all that much yourself.
rows.notes: Saburota answers Kusakabe that he remains much the same.

rows.en: Shut up! You traitor who has forgotten the spirit of the Jovian Federation!!
rows.notes: Shinjo condemns Saburota as betrayer of Jovian Federation spirit.

rows.en: Treason? Well, I suppose that's how you see it, Lieutenant General... But I like where I am now.
rows.notes: Saburota acknowledges Lieutenant General viewpoint then states liking present place.

rows.en: ...If that is your answer, come at me! We shall decide here whose ideals are right, yours or mine!
rows.notes: Kusakabe challenges Saburota to settle which of their ideals is correct.

rows.en: No, that was already decided... the moment the Nadesico C came here.
rows.notes: Saburota says outcome decided when Nadesico C arrived, answering previous challenge.

rows.en: Witch! If we shoot you down, control will return to us!
rows.notes: Shinjo threatens Ruri ship: shoot you down restores enemy control.

rows.en: Then victory will be ours!
rows.notes: Shinjo finishes prior conditional threat with their expected victory.

rows.en: ...I think your resistance is futile, though.
rows.notes: Ruri calmly tells Shinjo and Kusakabe resistance is futile.

rows.en: You never know who wins until the geta are on...!
rows.notes: Kusakabe uses footwear proverb about outcome remaining uncertain until end; retain geta anchor for reply.
uncertain: Cultural wordplay: source proverb uses geta footwear to mean the result is unknown until the end; literal anchor retained for row171.

rows.en: Then put them on right now. Geta, zori, sandals, whatever.
rows.notes: Ruri deliberately literalizes proverb: put footwear on now, geta/zori/sandals.
uncertain: Cultural wordplay: Ruri deliberately treats the geta proverb literally; geta and zori remain footwear terms.

rows.en: G-grrr!! Even if we perish, our convictions...!!
rows.notes: Shinjo growls and trails off asserting convictions even if faction perishes; incomplete source kept incomplete. Matching source fragment: remove the supplied auxiliary will so the unfinished boundary occurs at convictions, matching the source.
uncertain: Deliberate unfinished source fragment retained; do not supply a missing predicate about convictions.

rows.en: Any further resistance is pointless. Please surrender without a fight.
rows.notes: Ruri demands surrender in Kusakabe defeat handler after reused Kusakabe silence s0930:347.

rows.en: ...Understood...
rows.notes: Kusakabe complies with Ruri surrender demand in both defeat event and stage-ending event; generic response fits both.

rows.en: L-Lieutenant General Kusakabe!?
rows.notes: Shinjo reacts to Kusakabe accepting surrender in both events 10 and 11. Fixed Lieutenant General rank; stutter relocated onto English rank.

rows.en: We've been defeated once again. As the commander of the losing side, I refuse to disgrace myself any further.
rows.notes: Kusakabe explains surrender in both branches. Explicit we/I restored; defeated commander refuses further disgrace.

rows.en: L-Lieutenant General...
rows.notes: Shinjo trails off in an address to Kusakabe. Vocative, not an unfinished clause; fixed rank retained.

rows.en: Lieutenant Commander Hoshino... I want you to guarantee my subordinates' safety.
rows.notes: Kusakabe asks Ruri for a guarantee, not offering one. Fixed Lieutenant Commander Hoshino; I want you preserves request direction.

rows.en: ...Understood.
rows.notes: Ruri accepts Kusakabe's request to protect his subordinates. Acknowledgment has no dropped English clause.

rows.en: Hah... Hah... Hah...
rows.notes: Akito pants during the resolution branch. Breathing interjections, not unfinished clauses.

rows.en: ...Yurika...!
rows.notes: Akito calls Yurika's name. Vocative, not an unfinished clause.

rows.en: ...Any further resistance is pointless. Please surrender peacefully.
rows.notes: Ruri commands Kusakabe and Shinjo to surrender in event 11; polite imperative directed at listeners.

rows.en: Kazuya...! How long I've waited for this day...!
rows.notes: Erika greets Kazuya after his call in reused full-source row284. Explicit I restored.

rows.en: As I promised, I've returned to this planet. To hold you in my arms once again...
rows.notes: Kazuya returns to Mars as promised and embraces Erika; he rescued her, not vice versa. Purpose phrase follows complete first clause.

rows.en: I'm so glad... I'm so glad for you, big brother...!
rows.notes: Nana celebrates Kazuya's reunion. I restored; big brother is her familiar address, not a biological-relationship assertion.

rows.en: In the words of one who is gone: "Flowers return to their roots, birds to their old nests"...
rows.notes: Kyoshiro recalls words of a deceased person; no author named. Literal flowers/roots and birds/old nests return imagery retained.

rows.en: Our journey, which began on Mars, is finally coming to an end...
rows.notes: Kyoshiro reflects on their Mars-origin journey. Our journey restores subject; no place substituted.

rows.en: And he, too...
rows.notes: Kyoshiro turns to Akito's parallel homecoming; source deliberately leaves the predicate unfinished. Keep boundary and male referent from scene/profile.
uncertain: Unfinished source predicate intentionally retained: And he, too...; Akito referent inferred from adjacent Yurika rescue/return theme.

rows.en: ...Erika, how is Yurika Misumaru?
rows.notes: Kazuya asks Erika how Yurika is, leading to safe in190. Full name retained and interrogative predicate restored.

rows.en: She's safe. Right now, with everyone from the Nadesico...
rows.notes: Erika answers Kazuya. She restored for Yurika; second locative deliberately lacks final predicate in source, so remains unfinished.
uncertain: Unfinished source locative intentionally retained: Right now, with everyone from the Nadesico...

rows.en: ...Ugh... Unnh...
rows.notes: Yurika groans awake. Interjections, not a clause.
Silence retained in all nine original contexts.
Jun Aoi silently watches Yurika wake. Exact prefilled speaker retained; silence, not a clause.

rows.en: ...Huh... Everyone...?
rows.notes: Yurika recognizes the crew while waking. Huh/everyone are recognition interjection and address, not a dropped predicate.

rows.en: You all... look older...
rows.notes: Yurika's teasing observation to old friends; subject and look restored, no medical reading.

rows.en: What a relief... She's her usual ditzy self.
rows.notes: Minato is relieved Yurika is her usual ditzy self. She restored; no cognitive diagnosis.

rows.en: ...I... was dreaming all this time...
rows.notes: Yurika describes having dreamed throughout captivity. I and was restored; trailing pauses do not erase a complete clause.

rows.en: ...Akito...
rows.notes: Yurika calls for Akito. Vocative, not an unfinished clause.

rows.en: ...Where... is Akito...?
rows.notes: Yurika asks where Akito is. Complete English question restored.

rows.en: Goodby~e~...
rows.notes: Hikaru waves goodbye to departing Akito. Drawn-out farewell retained using allowed tilde.

rows.en: ...Wait, was it really right to let him go?
rows.notes: Hikaru asks companions whether letting Akito leave was right. Explicit him refers to Akito; impersonal it preserves ethical question.

rows.en: He says he's leaving. We can't force him to stay.
rows.notes: Saburota answers Hikaru: Akito chooses to leave and they cannot force him to stay. He/we actors restored.

rows.en: But... what's he going to do now...?
rows.notes: Ryoko wonders about Akito's future. He restored and question completed.

rows.en: Is he really going to leave like this... throwing away even Yurika and his memories with us...?
rows.notes: Ryoko asks whether Akito intends to abandon Yurika as well as memories with the crew. Explicit he/his restored; do not reduce to memories alone.

rows.en: He'll come back. If he doesn't... I'll just go after him.
rows.notes: Ruri reassures Ryoko that Akito will return, otherwise she will pursue him. He/I/him restored; no request-direction reversal.
uncertain: Japanese omits the pursuer and does not explicitly distinguish I from we. Ruri as speaker is rendered I; Akito as returning person is settled by199..203.

rows.en: Because he is...
rows.notes: Ruri's explanation stops at the row boundary before206. He/is restored but complement deliberately unfinished.
uncertain: Unfinished complement intentionally retained at row boundary;206 completes the explanation.

rows.en: Because he's someone precious to me...
rows.notes: Ruri completes the reason: Akito is precious. Personal valuation inferred from speaker; no reciprocal or romantic claim.
uncertain: Precious to me restores speaker-relative valuation; source does not explicitly state I versus collective we. No mutual romance asserted.

rows.en: You've done well to make it this far...! You've shown me the tenacity of a human being.
rows.notes: Conditional battle event12: Hokushin acknowledges Akito reaching him and human tenacity. It is not a resurrection after ending.

rows.en: ...Let's settle this...!
rows.notes: Conditional battle event12: Akito challenges Hokushin. Let's settle this gives complete challenge.

rows.en: A quick-draw shot? Laughable.
rows.notes: Conditional battle event12: Hokushin mocks a quick-draw gunshot. Explicit shot, never blade or sword.
